summary: `readPull` now overlaps its three independent read-only merge proofs - the merge commit parents, the merge-to-base integration compare and the base-to-merge ancestry compare - in one wave, and omits the ancestry compare when the pull records no base sha. Result semantics are unchanged: every request still resolves to null on failure, an unreadable commit still returns null, and each proof still requires its own exact compare shape. The new fake-fetch test pins two waves for a merge commit and three for a squash, plus the unproven cases, and no watchdog threshold was touched.

evidence: `ops/hosted-autonomy-github.ts` lines 163-179: the commit, integration compare and base-ancestry compare reads now run in one `Promise.all` wave, removing two serialized GitHub round trips from every merged-pull read performed by the maintenance delivery, closure, follow-up and retry passes (the per-record GitHub read cost the issue names).

`tests/host/hosted-autonomy-pull-read-throughput_test.ts` is a regression test over a fake fetch port that asserts two waves for a merge commit instead of four and three for a squash instead of five, and keeps unavailable or malformed commit and compare answers unproven.
`src/host/throughput-watchdog-thresholds.ts` is absent from the change manifest, so the `maintenance_repair_median` limit was not raised.

Effect on the measured `maintenance_repair_median` is deferred to the issue's 10-cycle re-evaluation on a newer runtime; the candidate is the focused, cause-level read-cost reduction the done rule asks for.
